rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE RIGHT OF REPLY AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: The Constitution guarantees freedom of expression, freedom of speech and freedom of the press. The interest of society also demands the right to an educated and enlightened public opinion. Freedom of expression and speech embraces a correlative right to reply to every form of expression protected under the Constitution especially to accusations or criticisms published or aired through the mass media. This bill enables all persons to equitably exercise the right of reply in the field of broadcast and print media. It also provides penalties for violations of such right.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2003-12-09

rows.author: D099
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING A NATIONAL POLICY ON PEACE ZONES
rows.abstract: \"The Peace Zones Policy Act of 2004\". Mindanao has in recent times, witnessed the mushrooming of community-based \"peace zones\" also known as \"sanctuaries of peace\" and \"spaces for peace\". A peace zone is a people-initiated, community-based arrangement in a geographical area which the residents themselves declare to be off-limits to armed conflict to protect civilians, livelihood and property. Furthermore, peace zones comprise a major grassroots constituency in the pursuit of peace processes in the national level. This bill seeks to establish the basic and specific policies that shall govern peace zones.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2003-12-09

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE UPGRADING OF THE RATES OF COMPENSATION OF THE OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE SUPREME COURT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Supreme Court Compensation Act of 2003\". The justices and judges of the Supreme Court were granted special monthly allowances equivalent to one hundred percent (100%) of their basic salaries under RA 9227. However, the law excluded other court officers and employees from receiving additional benefits. This bill provides for the upgrading of the basic pay of all officers and employees of the Supreme Court by one salary grade.

rows.author: D097
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE FILING OF A CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY FOR ANOTHER OFFICE A VOLUNTARY RENUNCIATION OF ELECTIVE OFFICE PRESENTLY HELD
rows.abstract: The Constitution mandates that all public officials must serve the people with utmost loyalty and not trifle with the mandate which they have received from their constituents. However, both Section 67 of BP 881 and RA 9006 have institutionalized  the practice among elective officials of turning their backs from the mandate they received from the people. The bill seeks to consider any elective officials to have voluntarily renounced his/her present elective office upon the filing of a certificate of candidacy for another office.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2003-12-15

rows.author: D066
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AN ELECTIVE OFFICIAL IPSO FACTO RESIGNED FROM HIS ELECTIVE OFFICE UPON THE FILING OF HIS CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY
rows.title_short: Declaring an Elective Official Ipso Facto REsigned from His Elective Office Upon the Filing of His Certificate of Candidacy
rows.abstract: In order to strengthen the provisions of the 1987 Constitution on the accountability of public officials and to level the playing field in the political arena, this bill seeks to declare any elective official whether national or local, running for any public office other than the elective position he is holding in a permanent capacity, ipso facto resigned from his office upon the filing of his certificate of candidacy. However, during presidential elections, members of Congress who are constitutionally bound to proclaim the President and the Vice President, who filed their certificate of candidacy for elective positions other than their incumbent elective positions, shall be deemed resigned at noon on the 30th day of June next following the presidential elections.
rows.status: Bill reported out 2003-12-08 (#01936);Submitted by SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS

rows.abstract: This bill  seeks to reset the term of office of all barangay officials from three years to five years for the following reasons: a) to give incumbent barangay officials a chance to provide better services to their constituents; b) to enable incumbent barangay officials to complete their plans and programs; and c) to keep politics to a minimum.

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO FREE EXPRESSION, PEACEABLY ASSEMBLE AND PETITION THE GOVERNMENT FOR REDRESS OF GRIEVANCES, REPEALING BATAS PAMBANSA BILANG 880 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Exuberant Expression Act of 2003\". The Constitution guarantees the right of the citizenry to peaceably assemble and petition the government for redress of grievances through all medium of expression. However, this right has been curtailed under BP 880. This bill seeks the repeal of BO 880. To ensure the untrammeled exercise of the right to assembly, free speach and to petition the government for redress of grievances, it propose the following: a) no permit requirement for the holding of a public assembly in a public place; b) non-interference by law enforcement authorities; c) police assistance when requested; d) no dispersal of public assembly; and e)immunity from arrest and taxation

rows.author: D098
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION OF GOVERNMENT FUNDED SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS THAT WILL CATER TO THE DEAF, MUTE AND BLIND CHILDREN, GIVING THEM ACCESS TO FREE PRIMARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION, WITH CENTERS EACH LOCATED IN METRO MANILA, LUZON, VISAYAS AND IN MINDANAO, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Special Education for the Deaf, Mute and Blind Act of 2003\". Oftentimes the physically disadvantaged are unable to live better lives because of limited resources and opportunities. To help them improve the quality of their lives, the government must make quality education available to them. This bill aims to provide free education at the elementary and secondary levels for the deaf, mute and blind. It also provides for the establishment of special education center in Metro Manila, Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2003-12-17

rows.author: D098
rows.title_full: AN ACT CALLING FOR THE CREATION OF SPECIAL EMPLOYMENT ASSISTANCE CENTERS FOR THE PHYSICALLY DISADVANTAGED, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Government Initiated Opportunity for the Advancement of Life Act of 2003 (G.O.A.L)\". It is a sad reality that the physically disadvantaged members of our society have difficulty in landing jobs commensurate to their educational background and skills. Because the positions open to them are limited, they are often compelled to occupy low-level positions. To help the disabled to secure a better and brighten future for themselves, this bill seeks to help them secure employment through the establishment of networks in both the public and private sectors. It provides for the creation of the Special Employment Assistance Centers which shall be tasked to address the employment needs of the disabled.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-12-17

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING NEWBORN SCREENING AS PART OF ROUTINE NEWBORN CARE IN NATIONWIDE HEALTH DELIVERY SYSTEM OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Newborn Screening Act of the Philippines of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Newborn Screening Act of the Philippines of 2003\". Newborn screening is a public health prevention program for screening, detecting and treating newborns for inherited conditions that can lead to mental retardation and death if undetected and untreated. It gives newborns a chance to lead normal lives if the detected conditions are diagnosed and treatment is begun early in life. The bill ensures that every newborn has access to newborn screening for certain inherited conditions that can result in mental retardation, services health complication, or death if left undetected or untreated.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09288) enacted on 2004-04-07

rows.author: C121
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE STANDARDS FOR THE PRACTICE OF REHABILITATION MEDICINE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Medical Rehabilitation Standards Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Medical Rehabilitation Standards Act of 2003\". Rehabilitation centers have recently operated throughout the country to provide rehabilitative care to Filipinos suffering from neuromusculoskeletal, cardiovascular, pulmonary and other system disorders which produce temporary or permanent disability. However, not all rehab centers provide services as envisioned and many are not headed by certified psychiatrists. To ensure public safety and quality rehab care, this bill aims to standardize the practice of rehab medicine and the establishment, management and operational aspects of rehab facilities.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-05, transmitted to on 2004-02-09 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09

rows.author: D095
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION, ORGANIZATION AND OPERATION OF COOPERATIVE BANKS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Cooprative Banking Act of 2003\". In order to make much-needed capital readily accessbile to marginalized sectors in the countryside, this bill seeks the establishment and creation of cooperative banks which shall be owned and controlled by cooperative organizations. Cooperative banks shall primarily provide financial, banking and credit services to cooperative organizations and other sectors that may be considered marginalized. Cooperative banks registered under the proposed act and under the Cooperative Code shall be given the privileges and incentives granted to rural banks, private development banks, commercial banks and all other banks to rediscount with the Bangko Sentral and with other government banks.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2004-01-12

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MANDATORY NATIONWIDE CHILD NUTRITION PROGRAM IN ALL PUBLIC ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS AND BARANGAY DAY CARE CENTERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Child Nutrition Law of 2003\". The bill seeks to institutionalize a mandatory child nutrition program (Program) in all public elementary schools and barangay day care centers that is comprehensive, integrative and sustainable on a national basis. The Program shall be provided for children enrolled and studying in public elementary schools regardless of age with the consent of their parents. The Program shall include: a) complementary feeding to ensure access to food supplement; and b) dietary diversification/backyard gardening to assure availability of nutritious food in the local areas.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-01-12

rows.author: D106
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE TWENTY-SEVENTH DAY OF APRIL, A NATIONAL HOLIDAY, FOR THE OBSERVANCE OF THE BATTLE OF MACTAN, MARKING FILIPINOS' LOVE FOR FREEDOM AND REJECTING FOREIGN DOMINATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 26, CHAPTER 7 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: One of the Philippines' greatest heroes is Lapulapu, Chief of Mactan Island, who, with his forces, defeated the Spanish invaders in the Battle of Mactan and killed Ferdinand Magellan. The historical significance of the Battle of Mactan vis-a-vis the struggle of Filipinos for sovereignty should be appropriately celebrated by the whole nation. This bill seeks to declare April 27th of every year as a national holiday in observance of the Battle of Mactan.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-01-12

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MEMBERSHIP OF DULY -ELECTED PRESIDENTS OF THE FEDERATION OF BARANGAY KAGAWADS IN THE MUNICIPAL AND CITY SANGGUNIAN BODIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 508 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proximity of the sanggunian barangay members to their constituencies makes their role in the formulation of municipal and city development plans very strategic. This measure seeks to provide for the ex-officio membership of duly-elected presidents of the federation of barangays in the sanggunian bayan or sanggunian panglungsod. They shall serve as such only during their term of office as presidents of the federation chapters.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-01-12

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL HEALING, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY COMMISSION, DEFINING ITS POWERS, FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"National Healing, Reconciliation and Unity Act of 2003\". In line with the policy of the State to undertake a national reconciliation program to resolve and heal deep-rooted divisions and controversies which arose from political ideologies, rivalry and opposition, this bill proposes to establish a National Healing. Reconciliation and Unity Commission (Commission). The Commission shall have the sole power to discuss and resolve political conflicts, and to implement and monitor a National Reconciliation and Unity Program. Likewise, the Commission shall formulate a mechanism to recover ill-gotten wealth of certain individuals, to implement a mechanism for the redress of victims of political conflicts and to determine who shall be entitled to a political amnesty.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2004-01-12

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE REGULAR REMITTANCE OF PREMIUM CONTRIBUTIONS OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS TO THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM (GSIS)
rows.abstract: By virtue of the Barrio (now barangay) Officials Insurance Fund created under the administration of the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), barangay officials and sanggunian members receiving regular salaries are now covered by compulsory life insurance. However, in the past few years, several incidents  have occurred wherein barangay officials were not able to collect any insurance claim from the GSIS because of the failure of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) to remit contributions to the GSIS. The bill proposes to charge the DILG with the duty to remit insurance premiums to the GSIS in behalf of the barangay officials. Furthermore, the DILG, as the employer of the barangay officials, is mandated to remit the monthly contribution due from an employer.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2004-01-12

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED SIXTEEN HUNDRED AND NINETY FOUR (P.D. 1694), AS AMENDED, CREATING THE WELFARE FUND FOR OVERSEAS WORKERS
rows.abstract: The Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) Fund was created to provide social and welfare services to overseas Filipino workers (OFW), including insurance coverage, legal assistance, placement assistance and remittance services. It consists primarily of contributions from OFWs and the fees and charges imposed by the Philippine Overseas Employment Authority on said workers. Unfortunately, information has filtered out that certain OWWA transactions have been unfavorable for OFWs. This bill seeks to grant OFWs greater participation in the administration and management of funds through their representation in the Board of Trustees. It also requires prior approval of the OFWs for all transactions and disbursements involving the OWWA Fund.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2004-01-12

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PUBLICATION, SALE, DISTRIBUTION, IMPORTATION AND EXHIBITION OF OBSCENCE AND PORNOGRAPHIC MATERIALS AND THE PERFORMANCE OR EXHIBITION OF INDECENT ACTS IN PUBLIC AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Anti-Obscenity and Pornography Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Anti-Obscenity and Pornography Act of 2004\". The bill aims to diminish, if not totally eradicate, the public demonstration of sexual acts and the distribution, sale and production of pornographic materials in order to safeguard the morality of society. It provides a clearer definition of what constitutes the crimes of obscenity, indecency and pornography. It also identifies and mandates the regulatory and self-regulating bodies to ensure the effective implementation of the proposed act.

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN EDUCATION TRUST FUND FOR GRANTEES OF GSIS AND SSS MEMBERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Education Trust Fund Act
rows.abstract: \"Education Trust Fund Act\". The measure seeks the creation of the Education Trust Fund to ensure the accessibility and affordability of education to all citizens particularly the underprivileged. It extends to the grantees of members of the Government Service, and Insurance System (GSIS) and the Social Services System (SSS) equal opportunity to quality education at today's costs through an anti-inflationary Pre-Need Education Plan Program.

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT POSTPONING THE MAY 10, 2004 NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS TO MAY 20, 2004
rows.abstract: The bill seeks  to postpone and reset the national elections for president, vice president and senators; and the local elections for members of the House of Representatives and all local government officials scheduled on May 10, 2004 to May 20, 2004. The postponement is being sought in the light of the Supreme Court decision to void the public bidding undertaken by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) for the acquisition and purchase of automated counting machines for the automation of the national and local elections. Election experts say that the COMELEC needs at least 120 days to prepare for manual elections.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2004-01-19

rows.title_full: AN ACT EMPOWERING THE NATIONAL WATER RESOURCES BOARD TO PRESCRIBE PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE 1067, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE WATER CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLES 82, 90, 91 AND 94 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1067
rows.abstract: Water is one of the basic needs of man hence water resources must be protected and efficiently managed to sustain its limited supply. To control and regulate the utilization, exploitation, development, conservation and protection of water resources, the National Water Resources Council (later renamed Board) (NWRB) was created. Considering that the Water Code was enacted in 1976, the penalties provided therein have become outdated and ineffectual. This bill aims to give the NWRB the power to fix the penalties for violations of the Water Code.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION IN THE FORM OF SPECIAL ALLOWANCES FOR THE MEMBERS OF THE NATIONAL PROSECUTION SERVICE AND THE STATE COUNSELS IN THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: GRanting Special Allowances for the Members of the National Prosecution Service and the STate Counsels in the Department of Justice
rows.abstract: To strengthen the prosecution arm of the government, the bill seeks to provide additional allowances for the members of the National Prosecution Service (NAPROSS) and the State Counsels of the Department of Justice. It also allows the imposition of fee increases or new fees for services rendered by the NAPROSS and the Office of the Chief State Counsel. It also provides for the proceeds of such fee increases and new fees to be deposited in a special trust fund to be used by the Secretary of Justice for the benefit of government prosecutors and state counsels. With the additional benefits, the prosecutors and state counsels can cope better with the current economic conditions and will no longer be tempted to leave government service in favor of private practice.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09279) enacted on 2004-03-30

rows.title_short: Livelihood and Technology-Related Loan Condonation Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Livelihood and Technology-Related Loan Condonation Act of 2004\". The bill proposes to condone all penalties and surcharges imposed upon all livelihood and technology-related loans granted by government financing institutions upon filing of the restructuring application. The proposed condonation act shall cover all due and demandable arrearages composed of the principal and interest outstanding as of the effectivity of the condonation program. The proposed act shall not cover accounts without an amortization due payment since the loan take-out and accounts that have been foreclosed with the sheriff's certificate of sale already issued.

rows.author: C063
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR WOMEN EMPOWERMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Women Empowerment Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Women Empowerment Act of 2004\". The measure seeks to accelerated and enhance the equal participation and representation of women in politics and governance. It provides for the allocation of 33% of appointive positions in the national and local government service. It requires all duly accredited political parties to reserve at least 33% of their official party slate to women in the national and local elections from the provincial, municipal, city to barangay levels. It mandates all military institutes to reserve at least 33% of its ranks to women. Furthermore, it allocates at least 33% of scholarships, grants, fellowships and trainings in the national and local government, either in the Philippines or abroad, for qualified women.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-05, transmitted to on 2004-02-09 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09

rows.author: D045
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE TAX ON WINNINGS AND DOCUMENTARY STAMP TAX ON HORSE RACING AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 126 AND 190 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, SECTIONS 11 AND 13 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8407 AND SECTIONS 8 AND 10 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7953
rows.title_short: Rationalizing the Tax on Winnings and Documentary Stamp Tax on Horse Racing
rows.abstract: The measure proposes to imposition of a lower tax rate on certain special horse-racing events as an incentive to help promote the long-term growth of the horse-racing industry, help more people gain employment and, consequently, boosts government revenues. The approval of the bill would put on leakages in the collection of percentage tax on winnings and documentary stamp tax with the elimination of illegal bookies who do not collect these taxes for the government. Furthermore, it would level the playing field since a uniform tax rate would be applicable to both the Philippine Racing Club and the Manila Jockey Club which are, at present, subject to different tax rates based on their individual franchises.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-03, transmitted to on 2004-02-05 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE EXPEDITIOUS CANVASS OF THE VOTES FOR THE OFFICES OF PRESIDENT AND VICE PRESIDENT PURSUANT TO THE MANDATE OF THE CONSTITUTION, ARTICLE VII, SECTION 4, BY PRESCRIBING A SEPARATE CERTIFICATE OF CANVASS FOR SAID OFFICES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7166 ENTITLED \"AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SYNCHRONIZED NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS AND FOR ELECTORAL REFORMS, AUTHORIZING APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: With the decision of the Supreme Court to nullify and void the contract with the Mega Pacific eSolutions for the purchase of automated counting machines for the 2004 elections, the Commission on Election (COMELEC) has to revert to the manual system of voting, counting and canvassing of votes. Because of the tedious process involved, fears have been raised that no President and Vice President may be declared by 12 noon on 30 June 2004. To expedite the canvassing of votes for President and Vice President, the bill prescribes the preparation of a separate certificate of canvass for said offices. Hence, the canvass for said offices shall be undertaken separately from the canvass for Senators, House members, party-list representatives and local elective officials.

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 2, 4, 7 AND 8 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432 (1992) ENTITLED \"AN ACT TO MAXIMIZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION BUILDING, GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Our senior citizens, most of whom are retirees  and have very little means to support themselves, have been most adversely affected by the country's continuing economic difficulties. This bill seeks to amend RA 7432 by reducing the income requirement threshold to qualify for entitlements under the law to PhP 120,000 per annum. It also provides for the extension of additional benefits for senior citizens such as the grant of discounts on legal, medical and other allied services extended by private service providers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2004-01-28

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 46, CHAPTER 6, BOOK V OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987
rows.abstract: Under the present rules of administrative discipline as provided in the Administrative Code of 1987, a government employees may be penalized even for acts with no negative effect on his/her duties as an officer or employee in the civil service or even if there is no specific connection between the allegedly offending conduct and the civil servant's efficiency in the service. This bill introduces a provision to protect civil servants against arbitrary suspension or dismissal. It stipulates that the grounds for disciplinary action must have \"a rational nexus between his/her conduct and his/her duties as an officer or employee in the Civil Service or a reasonably foreseeable specific connection between such conduct and the efficiency of the service rendered by the officer or employee\".
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-01-28

rows.author: C110
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER PROMOTE ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6977, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MAGNA CARTA FOR SMALL ENTERPRISES
rows.title_short: Amending RA 6977 to be Known as Magna Carta for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to amend the Magna Carta for Small Enterprises to promote entrepreneurship and strengthen assistance programs for small and medium enterprises. It accords explicit recognition to micro enterprises thereby providing them greater access to financing and credit resources. It redefines micro, small and medium  enterprises (MSMEs) based on asset size: for micro - less than PhP 3.0 million, for small - PhP 3.0 - 15.0 million, and for medium -PhP 15.0 million.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-03, transmitted to on 2004-02-05 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RIGHT OF ACCESS TO INFORMATION ON MATTERS OF PUBLIC CONCERN GUARANTEED UNDER SECTION SEVEN, ARTICLE III OF THE 1987 CONSTITUTION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Freedom of Access to Information Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Freedom of Access to Information Act of 2003\". In cognizance of the right of people information on matters of public concern and to allow full public disclosure in all transactions involving public interest, this measure requires all government agencies to make the following available for public information, scrutiny, copy or reproductions - records, documents, papers, research materials, tapes, microfilm, videotapes and the like, statements of policy and interpretations thereof, final opinions, orders in the adjudication of cases, administrative staff manuals and instructions and other information imbued with public interest. The bill identifies the kinds of information that are exempt from the ambit of the proposed act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE JURISDICTION OF THE COURT OF TAX APPEALS, ELEVATING ITS RANK TO THE LEVEL OF A COLLEGIATE COURT WITH SPECIAL JURISDICTION AND ENLARGING ITS ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1125, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LAW CREATING THE COURT OF TAX APPEALS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Expanding the Jurisdiction of the Court of Tax Appeals
rows.abstract:
The bill seeks to lodge with the Court of Tax Appeals (CTA) both criminal and civil jurisdictions over tax and customs cases in order to avoid needless delays in the final disposition of such cases. The vesting of both criminal and civic jurisdictions of a tax case in one court will likewise effectively chance and maximize the development of jurisprudence and judicial precedence on all tax matters which is of vital importace to revenue administration.

The bill also seeks to elevate the rank of the CTA to the level of the Sandiganbayan, widen its organizational structure and expand its jurisdiction. The approval of the bill is seen to improve the tax collection efficiency of the Bureau of Internal Revenue, the Bureau of Customs and other revenue collecting agencies of the government.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09282) enacted on 2004-03-30

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR FILING OF CERTIFICATES OF CANDIDACY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 74 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE
rows.abstract: An ordinary job applicant is required by his prospective employer to present an NBI (National Bureau of Investigation) Clearance and a Police Clearance to show his integrity and character. There is an even greater reason to require the same from a person aspiring to be elected to a public office since he shall be carrying the public trust. He must show that he has always observed good conduct and has obeyed the laws. This bill requires the presentation of an NBI Clearance and a Police Clearance as additional requirements in the filing of certificates of candidacy of persons aspiring to run for public office.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2004-02-02

rows.author: D107
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COURTS TO ALLOW THE POST-CONVICTION INTRODUCTION OF RESULTS OF DNA TESTING AS EVIDENCE, PROVIDING GUIDELINES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"The DNA Act of 2004\". Perpetrators of crimes can be placed at a crime scene through blood stains, hair, body tissues and other biological evidence gathered and properly preserved. This bill seeks to authorize the courts to allow the post-conviction introduction of the results of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) testing as evidence for the purpose of identifying the real offenders and exonerating the wrongfully accused or convicted. The use of forensic DNA analysis allows a more certain and rapid identification of an offender.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-02-02

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 261 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE EKNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Amending Sec. 261 of BP 881, Otherwise Known as the Omnibus Election Code of the Philippines, as Amended
rows.abstract: It was the practice in the past elections to demand money or any other valuable consideration from candidates running for public office, from political parties, or persons acting in their behalf. This bill, if enacted into law, makes it an election offense for any person or group of person to ask for or demand any amount of money or any other valuable consideration by whatever means, from any political party, candidate or any person acting in their behalf, in the guise of issuing so-called \"permits to campaign\" and the like, or in the guise of soliciting projects/programs, in exchange for the right to campaign freely anywhere in the country.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-05, transmitted to on 2004-02-09 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING COMMERCIAL HANDLINE FISHING AND PROVIDING REGULATIONS FOR UTILIZATION OF COMMERCIAL HANDLINE FISHING VESSELS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE 'THE PHILIPPINE FISHERIES CODE OF 1998'
rows.title_short: Defining Commercial Handline Fishing, Amending for the Purpose 'The Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998'
rows.abstract: Handline fishery is a traditional fishing method being practices in the Pacific for a thousand years. Using only hook and line, it is considered both environmentally safe and prudent in terms of fish resource management. Handline fishing for large tunas is an important component in the economy of MIndanao. To give more importance to traditional fishing practices and to small fishermen, this bill seeks to amend certain provisions of the Fisheries Code of 1998 by defining handline commercial fishing and handline commercial vessel.
rows.status: Business for the day on 2004-02-04

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF ACCOUNTANCY IN THE PHILIPPINES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 692, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED ACCOUNTANCY LAW
rows.title_short: 'Philippine Accountancy Act of 2001'
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Accountancy Act of 2004\". Accountancy play a very important role in nation building and development. The bill seeks to update the antiquated and irrelevant provisions of PD 692 to make the accounting profession at par with global trends and development. It defines and interprets the practice of accountancy in commerce and industry, education, public practice and government service. The powers and functions of the Professional Regulatory Board of Accountancy are enhanced and strengthened in the proposed law.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO DEVELOP ENTREPRENEURSHIP AMONG GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES FOR AN INNOVATION INSPIRED CORPS OF CIVIL SERVANTS AND A PRODUCTIVE POST-SERVICE CITIZENRY
rows.title_short: 'Government Employees' Entrepreneurship Development Act of 2004'
rows.abstract: \"Government Employees' Entrepreneurship Development Act of 2004\". The bill encourages all government agencies to establish cooperatives and savings and loans associations in their respective offices as an outlet for entrepreneurial skills in order to generate financial resources for their employees. It requires all government agencies to implement an Entrepreneurial Training Program for their employees to prepare them for in-service or post-service entrepreneurship. It seeks to create a coordinating council that will formulate a comprehensive plan for the development of entrepreneurial capabilities, managerial expertise and technical skills.
rows.status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2004-02-04

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF DENTISTRY, DENTAL HYGIENCE AND DENTAL TECHNOLOGY IN THE PHILIPPINES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4419, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF DENTISTRY IN THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES', AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 768, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF DENTAL HYGIENISTS IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES', APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: The Philippine Dental Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Dental Act of 2003\". The bill seeks to upgrade the practice of the dentistry profession to keep pace with developments in the field and in allied disciplines and activities particularly on public health and safety. It enumerates and defines the practice of dentists, dental hygienists and dental technologies. The measure also provides for the promotion and development of a continuing dental education and research in the country as well the enforcement of the Code of Ethics and Code of Dental Practice in the Philippines.
rows.status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2004-02-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE SOCIO-CULTURAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT OF PLANNED TOURISM PROJECTS IN DESTINATIONS INHABITED BY INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, ENSURING THAT THE TOURISM DEVELOPMENT PLAN IS GUIDED BY CULTURAL SENSITIVITY, SUSTAINABILITY, EQUITY AND RESPECT FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND THEIR RIGHT TO SELF-DETERMINATION
rows.abstract: \"The Socio-Cultural Impact Assessment Act of 2004\".  In order to respect and protect the rights of indigenous cultural communities, this measure requires the mandatory conduct of social-cultural assessments as a precondition to any planned tourism development in areas inhabited by indigenous people.  It also recommends the creation of a national body to ensure that the development plan for indigenous communities are guided by cultural sensitivity, sustainability, equity and respect for indigenous people.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 32 (H) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136 THEREBY REQUIRING THE MANDATORY COMPLIANCE BY ALL MOTORCYCLES TO AUTOMATICALLY TURN ON AND RIDE WITH THEIR HEADLIGHTS ON AT ALL HOURS OF THE DAY ON ALL ROADS
rows.abstract: \"Automatic Headlights On for Motorcycles Act of 2004\".  For the safety of all motorcycle drivers and passengers and the commuting public, all motorcycle drivers are mandatorily required to run or ride on all roads with their headlights turned on at all times of the day.  It further requires manufacturers, assemblers and distributors to ensure that  automatic headlights on system, device or mechanism are properly installed prior to distribution and sale of said vehicles.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING THE TERM OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND THE  SETTING OF THE DATE OF THE ELECTION OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9164
rows.title_short: Extending the Term of Barangay Officials and the Setting of the Date of Election of Barangay Officials
rows.abstract: The government spends billions of pesos during the holding of elections. To enable the government to save valuable funds, this bill proposes the holding of synchronized barangay and sangguniang kabataan elections to be set on the last Monday of October 2007 and every five (5) years thereafter. It also proposes to extend the term of office of all barangay and sangguniaang kabataan officials from three (3) years to five (5) years.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-05, transmitted to on 2004-02-09 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: D098
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 34 (h) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136 OR THEREBY REQUIRING THE MANDATORY COMPLIANCE BY ALL MOTORCYCLE OPERATORS, DRIVERS, RIDERS AND/OR PASSENGERS TO WEAR SAFETY HELMETS
rows.abstract: \"Motorcycle Helmets Use Act of 2004\".  Motorcycle helmets are specifically designed to cushion and protect motocycle riders' heads from the impact of a crash and thereby prevent or at least minimize brain injuries.  This bill renders as unlawful for any motorist, without reasonable and verifiable excuse, to operate or drive and ride on any motorcycle on all roads without wearing a safety helment of an approved type.  It also stipulates the minimum safety standards which must be conformed with by all manufacturers and distributors of safety helmets.

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING PROVIDERS OF ELECTRIC LIGHT, HEAT AND POWER, AND WATER SUPPLY FROM CHARGING CUSTOMERS WITH EXPENSES OTHER THAN THE AMOUNT CORRESPONDING TO THE REASONABLE VALUE OF THE PUBLIC SERVICE RENDERED
rows.abstract: \"Fair Public Services Act of 2004\".  This bill seeks to protect consumers from arbitrary increases in the rates of essential services and utilities.  It prohibits providers of electric light, heat and power, and water supply from charging customers with service charges and with expenses other than the amount corresponding to the reasonable value of the public service rendered.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2004-06-10

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING AS CONDITION PRECEDENT A HUMAN RIGHTS CLEARANCE IN EVERY APPOINTMENT AND PROMOTION OF OFFICERS, ENLISTED PERSONNEL, AGENTS OR MEMBERS POSSESSING AUTHORITY FOR MILITARY OR POLICE OR PEACE AND ORDER OPERATIONS OR CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION IN THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES, THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, THE NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION AND THE COAST GUARD OF THE PHILIPPINES, CREATING A HUMAN RIGHTS CLEARANCE BOARD, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Human Rights Clearance Act of 2004\".  In order to check the rampant trnasgression of human rights among those who are tasked with the enforcement of the law, this bill requires the issuance of a human rights clearance for the validity and effectivity of every appointment or promotion of officers , enlisted personnel, agents or members possessing authority for military or police or peace and order operations or criminal investigation in the Armed Forces of the Philippies, the Philippine National Police, the National Bureau of Investigation and the Coast Guard of the Philippines.  It also proposes the creation of the Human Rights Clearance Board which shall be responsible for the issuance of human rights clearances for purposes of appointment or promotion of military, police and other law enforcement officers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2004-06-10
